images.title: Odd plus even always leaves one unpaired
images.purpose: Shows that an odd number plus an even number is odd, so it can never be a multiple of 6, which is even.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no characters, no extra text. Three dot pictures in pairs, in one row, with a plus sign and an equals sign between them.
images.exact_structure: Picture 1: 3 pairs of teal (#0072B2) dots in two rows and 1 extra amber (#E69F00) dot at the end, 7 dots, labelled 7 above. A plus sign. Picture 2: 4 pairs of teal (#0072B2) dots in two rows, 8 dots, labelled 8 above. An equals sign. Picture 3: 7 pairs of teal (#0072B2) dots in two rows and 1 extra amber (#E69F00) dot at the end, 15 dots, labelled 15 above. A reddish purple (#CC79A7) ring around the extra dot in picture 3 with the label 1 left unpaired under it. Under the whole row, centred: never a multiple of 6. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Odd plus even always has one dot left unpaired, so it is odd and never a multiple of 6.
images.description: Shows that an odd number plus an even number is odd, so it can never be a multiple of 6, which is even.
images.context: 7 + 8 = 15, odd; every multiple of 6 is 6j = 2 × 3j, even.

image_decisions.why: Pairing dots shows the odd leftover directly, which is the reason the statement is never true.
